Examples: "How does taint analysis work here?", "Why didn't explain find this flow?", "Add a new sink/source", "Review the interprocedural taint code".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". content.text:
Search complete. Here are my definitive findings.

## 1. Does any rate-limiting middleware exist? — No.

There is **no API rate-limiting middleware anywhere in the memos repository** — not in the Go backend, not in the web frontend, and not in config. I searched exhaustively for `rate limit`, `ratelimit`, `rate-limit`, `throttle`, `limiter`, `requests per`, `RPS`, `quota`, token/leaky/sliding bucket, `429`, `too many requests`, and every common Go rate-limiting library (`x/time/rate`, `tollbooth`, `ulule/limiter`, `throttled`, `sethvargo/go-limiter`). None are used.

## 2. The actual middleware/interceptor chain (no rate limiter present)

The server uses Connect/gRPC interceptors, registered in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-141`:

```go
connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
    NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
    NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
)
connectHandler.RegisterConnectHandlers(connectMux, connectInterceptors, connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes))
```

The four interceptors are all defined in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go` (Metadata, Logging, Recovery, Auth). **None of them is a rate limiter.** There is no throttling interceptor to add.

## 3. Per-user rate limiting — Does not exist.

There is no per-user (or per-IP, or global) request rate limiting at all. The only per-user logic in the codebase is authorization/ownership checks (e.g. `memo.CreatorID != user.ID && !isSuperUser(user)`), not throttling.

## What does exist (related but NOT rate limiting)

These are the only "limit"-style protections, and none of them limit request frequency:

- **Request body size cap** — `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20`: `const maxAPIRequestBytes = 256 << 20` (256 MB), enforced via `http.MaxBytesHandler` (lines 126, 144) and `connect.WithReadMaxBytes` (line 141). This is a payload-size limit, not a request-rate limit.
- **Concurrency semaphore for thumbnails** — `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59`: `semaphore.NewWeighted(3)` limiting concurrent thumbnail generation (used in `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:427-447`). Concurrency guard, not rate limiting.
- **Pagination limits** — e.g. `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/common.go:49-55`, `user_service_stats.go:96,233`. Page-size clamps only.
- **Doc-comment mention only** — `/bench/home/work/internal/email/doc.go:86`: `//   - Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse`. This is a security-best-practice suggestion in a package doc comment; the email package (`internal/email/`) implements **no** rate limiting.
- **`golang.org/x/time` in `go.mod:151`** — marked `// indirect` (transitive dependency). Confirmed it is **not imported by any `.go` file** in the repo, so its `rate` package is not used.

**Conclusion:** memos has no API rate-limiting middleware and no per-user rate limiting. Adding it would mean writing a new Connect interceptor and inserting it into the chain at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133`.
